title: Open Code Review
body:
CodeRabbit Essentials costs $24 per developer a month if you pay for the year. For a team of ten that's $240 every month.

Open Code Review is a CLI that reads your Git diffs, and an LLM agent writes review comments on the exact lines. The README says Alibaba used it internally first. You still need your own model endpoint and you pay for the tokens yourself. They also say recall is lower on purpose.

The repo has 222 contributors and someone committed today.
verdict: I think a team that's fine with a CLI and already pays for an LLM API doesn't need to keep paying for CodeRabbit.

facts.description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
facts.price_quote: or $24 per developer per month when billed annually
facts.readme_excerpt: OpenCodeReview                                                                                        English |  简体中文  |  日本語  |  한국어  |  Русский    --- ## What is Open Code Review? Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, `ocr scan` reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff. Visit the [official website](https://open-codereview.ai) for more details.   ## Benchmark > Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), Open Code Review achieves significantly higher **Precision** and **F1** with the same underlying model, while consuming only **~1/9 of the tokens** and completing reviews faster. Note that its Recall is lower than general-purpose agents — a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise. A r

intro: Alibaba's command-line tool that has an LLM review your Git diffs, for teams that want code review done automatically.

title: Jarvis
body:
Wispr Flow Pro is $12 per user a month. For a team of ten that's $120 every month.

Jarvis is a local voice assistant and its description calls it a free Wispr Flow alternative with dictation. Dictation is only one of a lot of features in it. The README says the speech and chat models run locally when you use a local model server, so you have to set that up and keep it running.

Eleven people have worked on it and the last commit was today.
verdict: Before you cancel Wispr Flow, use them side by side for a bit. This one is mostly an assistant, and the dictation is the smaller part of it.

facts.description: A 100% private and local AI assistant for your desktop. Always present, able to jump into conversations. Supports unlimited MCP tools and unlimited memory with self-learning. Free WisprFlow alternative with its dictation support. Runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.
facts.readme_excerpt: # Jarvis ### Your intelligence. Your hardware. A private, local-first AI assistant with voice and text chat.  Talk naturally, as if Jarvis were a third person in the room. **Voice-first · Local AI · Personal memory · No subscription** [**Download Jarvis →**](https://github.com/isair/jarvis/releases)   ·   [Website](https://barissencan.com/jarvis/)   ·   [Get started](#quick-install)   ·   [Explore the app](#inside-jarvis)   ·   [Support the project](#support)   --- ## An assistant that lives with you, not in the cloud Jarvis is built to be part of the conversation. Talk through an idea, discuss plans with a friend, then ask “Jarvis, what do you think?” While listening, it keeps a short, temporary rolling transcript of nearby speech so it can join an ongoing conversation using what was just discussed. Address Jarvis by name anywhere in a sentence and follow up naturally. Speech recognition, language models and speech synthesis run on hardware you control. Your diary and knowledge graph stay on your computer. Speech and chat models run locally when you use a local model server. Sensitive information is redacted before reaching model context or the saved diary. Web search, weather and connected tools use the network for those requests.         A voice, a face, and a place in the conversation.   ## Quick Install **1. Download the app.** Choose your platform from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/isair/jarvis/releases). | Platform | Pac

intro: A desktop AI assistant you talk to by voice, and the dictation and chat run on your own computer, so it stays private.

title: SupoClip
body: SupoClip's README starts with "Fuck OpusClip." OpusClip's Starter plan is $15 a month. You give SupoClip a long video, it picks the moments it scores as most viral and cuts them into vertical clips with subtitles. You run it yourself with Docker Compose on your own hardware, and the README says there's no usage limit then. If you don't want to set it up there's a hosted version too. Eight people have worked on it and the last commit was today.
verdict: If you can run Docker Compose, you can cancel OpusClip Starter.

facts.readme_excerpt: Fuck OpusClip.    ... because good video clips shouldn't come with ugly watermarks or platform lock-in.                                     --- SupoClip is an open-source, AI-powered video clipping tool. Give it a long video — a podcast, a talk, a stream VOD — and it finds the most viral-worthy moments, scores them, and renders them as vertical 9:16 clips with face-centered cropping, word-synced subtitles, hook titles, and optional B-roll. Run it yourself, customize it, inspect it — or use the hosted version and skip the setup. **See it first:** [watch real clips SupoClip generated](https://www.supoclip.com/demo) from a long-form interview, or follow the [self-hosting tutorial](https://www.supoclip.com/blog/self-host-supoclip-docker) to run it on your own machine. ## Ways to Use SupoClip | Option | Details | |---|---| | **Hosted web app** | [www.supoclip.com](https://www.supoclip.com) — no infrastructure to run | | **iOS app** | [SupoClip on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/supoclip/id6784760040) — the same hosted pipeline, from your iPhone | | **Self-host** | Docker Compose setup below, or the step-by-step [self-hosting tutorial](https://www.supoclip.com/blog/self-host-supoclip-docker) — AGPL-3.0, unlimited usage on your own hardware | | **MCP server** | [`mcp/`](mcp/) — use SupoClip from Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients | | **REST API** | API keys from `/settings/api-keys` authenticate the backend directly — see the [API reference](docs/api-

intro: Open-source tool that cuts long videos like podcasts and streams into vertical clips, for people who post shorts.

title: Mailflare
body: Google Workspace Starter is €6.80 per user a month. Mailflare is self-hosted email and calendar on your own domain, and the README says it runs on Cloudflare or Docker. You still pay for a sending service like Resend or Amazon SES, and for somewhere to keep the files. It has 54 contributors and the last commit was today.
verdict: If your team is fine running its own mail on Cloudflare, you can cancel Workspace.

facts.readme_excerpt: # Mailflare A self-hosted alternative to Google Workspace. Setup **custom domain Emails**, **Calendar, Drive, Booking** and **built-in AI agents**. Run it on Cloudflare or Docker. Send and receive with Cloudflare, Resend or Amazon SES. Store files in R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3. Use D1, Postgres, MySQL or Turso for the database. Attendees get email invitations. - **Booking**: Share a public link so anyone can book a free time on your calendar. - **Drive**: Store and share files. - **AI agents**: Search mail, draft replies and manage events. intro: Self-hosted email for teams who want mail on their own domain, with calendar and file storage in the same place.
